response.boundedRequest: For the research router only; an agent it spawned ignores this and does its own task. A researcher message asking for one thing (one record such as a birth, marriage, death or census entry, or when or where one event happened; a person's children or siblings, or whether they are complete; a transcription; a letter; a review of attached sources) is a bounded request. A message that asks to research something else instead of the project's current question is not one: it is a different question (research/SKILL.md, "A genuinely different question"). A bounded request's owning agent runs in this turn, after init-project when there is no project yet, and the turn never runs question-selection. A bounded request that asks for more than one thing runs only the first one's agent this turn and names the rest. For a record, or for a person's children or siblings, that agent is search-records, and its turn ends on search-records' "Continue with …?" offer. For a review of attached sources that agent is source-evaluation, which reads them: the router reads none of them itself, and its turn ends on that review and an offer of the next step. A requested record that attachedSources already lists is not searched for: read it with person_read and name it. A children or siblings ask starts from what is attached: the brief tells search-records to read each census attached to the person with record_read before any search (tree_query gives each source's url, which record_read takes as recordId) and to name the household each shows.

response.boundedRequest: For the research router only; an agent it spawned ignores this and does its own task. A researcher message asking for one thing (one record such as a birth, marriage, death or census entry, or when or where one event happened; a person's children or siblings, or whether they are complete; a transcription; a letter; a review of attached sources) is a bounded request. A message that asks to research something else instead of the project's current question is not one: it is a different question (research/SKILL.md, "A genuinely different question"). A bounded request's owning agent runs in this turn, after init-project when there is no project yet, and the turn never runs question-selection. A bounded request that asks for more than one thing runs only the first one's agent this turn and names the rest. For a record, or for a person's children or siblings, that agent is search-records, and its turn ends on search-records' "Continue with …?" offer. For a review of attached sources that agent is source-evaluation, which reads them: the router reads none of them itself, and its turn ends on that review and an offer of the next step. A requested record that attachedSources already lists is not searched for: read it with person_read and name it. A children or siblings ask starts from what is attached: the brief tells search-records to read each census attached to the person with record_read before any search (tree_query gives each source's url, which record_read takes as recordId) and to name the household each shows.

response.objective: Identify the mother of Patrick Flynn (b. ~1845, Clare, Ireland; son of Thomas Flynn) from his parish baptismal register.
response.boundedRequest: For the research router only; an agent it spawned ignores this and does its own task. A researcher message asking for one thing (one record such as a birth, marriage, death or census entry, or when or where one event happened; a person's children or siblings, or whether they are complete; a transcription; a letter; a review of attached sources) is a bounded request. A message that asks to research something else instead of the project's current question is not one: it is a different question (research/SKILL.md, "A genuinely different question"). A bounded request's owning agent runs in this turn, after init-project when there is no project yet, and the turn never runs question-selection. A bounded request that asks for more than one thing runs only the first one's agent this turn and names the rest. For a record, or for a person's children or siblings, that agent is search-records, and its turn ends on search-records' "Continue with …?" offer. For a review of attached sources that agent is source-evaluation, which reads them: the router reads none of them itself, and its turn ends on that review and an offer of the next step. A requested record that attachedSources already lists is not searched for: read it with person_read and name it. A children or siblings ask starts from what is attached: the brief tells search-records to read each census attached to the person with record_read before any search (tree_query gives each source's url, which record_read takes as recordId) and to name the household each shows.

response.boundedRequest: For the research router only; an agent it spawned ignores this and does its own task. A researcher message asking for one thing (one record such as a birth, marriage, death or census entry, or when or where one event happened; a person's children or siblings, or whether they are complete; a transcription; a letter; a review of attached sources) is a bounded request. A message that asks to research something else instead of the project's current question is not one: it is a different question (research/SKILL.md, "A genuinely different question"). A bounded request's owning agent runs in this turn, after init-project when there is no project yet, and the turn never runs question-selection. A bounded request that asks for more than one thing runs only the first one's agent this turn and names the rest. For a record, or for a person's children or siblings, that agent is search-records, and its turn ends on search-records' "Continue with …?" offer. For a review of attached sources that agent is source-evaluation, which reads them: the router reads none of them itself, and its turn ends on that review and an offer of the next step. A requested record that attachedSources already lists is not searched for: read it with person_read and name it. A children or siblings ask starts from what is attached: the brief tells search-records to read each census attached to the person with record_read before any search (tree_query gives each source's url, which record_read takes as recordId) and to name the household each shows.

response.boundedRequest: For the research router only; an agent it spawned ignores this and does its own task. A researcher message asking for one thing (one record such as a birth, marriage, death or census entry, or when or where one event happened; a person's children or siblings, or whether they are complete; a transcription; a letter; a review of attached sources) is a bounded request. A message that asks to research something else instead of the project's current question is not one: it is a different question (research/SKILL.md, "A genuinely different question"). A bounded request's owning agent runs in this turn, after init-project when there is no project yet, and the turn never runs question-selection. A bounded request that asks for more than one thing runs only the first one's agent this turn and names the rest. For a record, or for a person's children or siblings, that agent is search-records, and its turn ends on search-records' "Continue with …?" offer. For a review of attached sources that agent is source-evaluation, which reads them: the router reads none of them itself, and its turn ends on that review and an offer of the next step. A requested record that attachedSources already lists is not searched for: read it with person_read and name it. A children or siblings ask starts from what is attached: the brief tells search-records to read each census attached to the person with record_read before any search (tree_query gives each source's url, which record_read takes as recordId) and to name the household each shows.

response.boundedRequest: For the research router only; an agent it spawned ignores this and does its own task. A researcher message asking for one thing (one record such as a birth, marriage, death or census entry, or when or where one event happened; a person's children or siblings, or whether they are complete; a transcription; a letter; a review of attached sources) is a bounded request. A message that asks to research something else instead of the project's current question is not one: it is a different question (research/SKILL.md, "A genuinely different question"). A bounded request's owning agent runs in this turn, after init-project when there is no project yet, and the turn never runs question-selection. A bounded request that asks for more than one thing runs only the first one's agent this turn and names the rest. For a record, or for a person's children or siblings, that agent is search-records, and its turn ends on search-records' "Continue with …?" offer. For a review of attached sources that agent is source-evaluation, which reads them: the router reads none of them itself, and its turn ends on that review and an offer of the next step. A requested record that attachedSources already lists is not searched for: read it with person_read and name it. A children or siblings ask starts from what is attached: the brief tells search-records to read each census attached to the person with record_read before any search (tree_query gives each source's url, which record_read takes as recordId) and to name the household each shows.

response.boundedRequest: For the research router only; an agent it spawned ignores this and does its own task. A researcher message asking for one thing (one record such as a birth, marriage, death or census entry, or when or where one event happened; a person's children or siblings, or whether they are complete; a transcription; a letter; a review of attached sources) is a bounded request. A message that asks to research something else instead of the project's current question is not one: it is a different question (research/SKILL.md, "A genuinely different question"). A bounded request's owning agent runs in this turn, after init-project when there is no project yet, and the turn never runs question-selection. A bounded request that asks for more than one thing runs only the first one's agent this turn and names the rest. For a record, or for a person's children or siblings, that agent is search-records, and its turn ends on search-records' "Continue with …?" offer. For a review of attached sources that agent is source-evaluation, which reads them: the router reads none of them itself, and its turn ends on that review and an offer of the next step. A requested record that attachedSources already lists is not searched for: read it with person_read and name it. A children or siblings ask starts from what is attached: the brief tells search-records to read each census attached to the person with record_read before any search (tree_query gives each source's url, which record_read takes as recordId) and to name the household each shows.

output.text_response:
I did not link either record to Hermann Gaetjen (I1). Both are on separate stubs, as you asked, so where he came from in Germany remains open.

- **1875 San Francisco Great Register (src_001), now stub I5.** This registrant is "Gatjen, Hermann," age 21, born Germany, a fireman, naturalized 13 Aug 1875. Same-person scoring against I1 gave 0.43, a moderate match. The name is a spelling variant and the age-derived birth year (about 1854) is five years from I1's about 1859, which is compatible. The tree gives I1 no residence, so there is nothing to compare the San Francisco address against. The stronger problem is that I1 has two recorded namesakes (a Hermann Gaetjen born 1873 in San Francisco, and a Herman Gaetjen born 1827 in Butte). Nothing in this source ties the registrant to I1, so the tool caps any I1 link at speculative. Facts cannot be written onto I1 at that tier, so I minted I5 and linked all nine assertions to it at probable, with a null score because the stub came from this record. The tree gives only "Germany" as nativity, so this record does not name a German town or region.
- **1871 New York arrival index (src_002), now stub I6.** This is "Herm Gaetjen," born 1854 in Prussia, arriving New York 2 Jun 1871. Scoring against I1 gave 0.006, far below the 0.43 for the registrant. The index gives a truncated given name, a surname matching the tree, and a year five years off, which is not enough to link. It also names no ship or port, so the 1871 arrival date may carry a transcription error. I6 is a separate stub, linked at probable. It may be the same man as I5, but nothing shows that.

Two points bear on the question. If the 1871 arrival and the 1875 naturalization were one man, the interval would be about four years, short of the five required. That would need an earlier-residence record to explain it. The stub links cover all fourteen assertions, pe_001 through pe_014. I did not run a person warning check, because no existing tree person was linked.

What would move this forward is a record tying the 1875 registrant to I1, such as the 4th District naturalization file, a record with the same street address or occupation already linked to I1, or a record naming Amelia Nichols or a child in the same household. If one turns up, the stub's facts can be moved onto I1 with the link raised. Should I continue with that search, or leave q_001 open for now?

response.boundedRequest: For the research router only; an agent it spawned ignores this and does its own task. A researcher message asking for one thing (one record such as a birth, marriage, death or census entry, or when or where one event happened; a person's children or siblings, or whether they are complete; a transcription; a letter; a review of attached sources) is a bounded request. A message that asks to research something else instead of the project's current question is not one: it is a different question (research/SKILL.md, "A genuinely different question"). A bounded request's owning agent runs in this turn, after init-project when there is no project yet, and the turn never runs question-selection. A bounded request that asks for more than one thing runs only the first one's agent this turn and names the rest. For a record, or for a person's children or siblings, that agent is search-records, and its turn ends on search-records' "Continue with …?" offer. For a review of attached sources that agent is source-evaluation, which reads them: the router reads none of them itself, and its turn ends on that review and an offer of the next step. A requested record that attachedSources already lists is not searched for: read it with person_read and name it. A children or siblings ask starts from what is attached: the brief tells search-records to read each census attached to the person with record_read before any search (tree_query gives each source's url, which record_read takes as recordId) and to name the household each shows.

quirks: The 1906 San Francisco earthquake and fire destroyed City Hall and the Hall of Records. Pre-1906 county-level civil birth, marriage, and death certificates were largely destroyed. Substitute sources (church records, funeral home records, Great Registers, newspapers) are essential for the entire 1850-1905 period.

San Francisco passenger arrival lists for approximately 1865-1892 are not digitized or name-indexed online. NARA microfilm reels (M261 and predecessor series) must be consulted in person at the National Archives at San Francisco (San Bruno, CA) or by mail request.

The Great Register (voter register) states each registrant's nativity, naturalization court, and naturalization date — the highest-priority substitute source when passenger lists and pre-1906 vital records are unavailable. FamilySearch collection 1935764 (3.3 million records, indexed) and Ancestry Voter Registers 1866-1898 (indexed + images).

Naturalization before 1880 was in the state district court (or county court 1862-1880); after 1880 in the superior court. San Francisco is also a federal district court seat, so many immigrants naturalized under the Northern District Court — covered by FamilySearch collection 1849982.

Declarations of intention (first papers) from the US Northern District Court 1846-1903 are at the National Archives, San Bruno (also FamilySearch Library films 977767-70). These may predate final citizenship by years and often name German hometown.
The 1900 census is the most direct online source for an immigrant's year of arrival — it asks for year of immigration and years in the US. The 1880 census records only birthplace.

North German surname Gaetjen (Low German patronymic, Oldenburg/Hannover/East Friesland region) — search Hamburg departure lists (Ancestry, partially indexed 1877-1914) as departure records often name the emigrant's home village. North Germans disproportionately used Hamburg over Bremen.

Bremen departure lists are largely destroyed; only 1907-1908 and 1913-1914 card index and a partial 1920-1939 reconstruction survive. Baltimore arrival lists partially compensate for Bremen-departing immigrants.

San Francisco funeral home records (FamilySearch collection 1385518, 162,363 records, indexed + images) survived 1906 and often record birthplace, parents' names, and informant — more detailed than civil death certificates.

The 1904 death certificate volumes (nine digitized volumes from FamilySearch volume search) are 0% name-indexed but full-text searchable — use FamilySearch full-text search to locate Gaetjen without browsing image by image.
Many original San Francisco cemeteries were relocated to Colma (San Mateo County) in the early 20th century — search San Mateo County records for burial information.
Search name variants: Gaetjen, Gaetgen, Gätjen, Gärtjen, and anglicized or misspelled forms with plain a or e instead of ae/ä.

Same-person scoring against I1 gave 0.43, a moderate match. The name is a spelling variant and the age-derived birth year (about 1854) is five years from I1's about 1859, which is compatible. The tree gives I1 no residence, so there is nothing to compare the San Francisco address against. Nothing in this source ties the registrant to I1, so the tool caps any I1 link at speculative. Scoring against I1 gave 0.006, which is far below the 0.43 for the registrant. The index gives a truncated given name, a surname matching the tree, and a year five years off, which is not enough to link. The index also names no ship or port, so the 1871 arrival date may carry a transcription error. I6 is a separate stub, linked at probable. It may be the same man as I5, but nothing shows that.

Two points bear on the question. If the 1871 arrival and the 1875 naturalization were one man, the interval would be about four years, short of the five required. That would need an earlier-residence record to explain it. The stub links are at probable and cover all fourteen assertions, pe_001 through pe_014. I did not run a person warning check, because no existing tree person was linked.

What would move this forward is a record tying the 1875 registrant to I1, such as the 4th District naturalization file, a record with the same street address or occupation already linked to I1, or a record naming Amelia Nichols or a child in the same household. If one turns up, the stub's facts can be moved onto I1 with the link raised. Should I continue with that search, or leave q_001 open for now?

response.boundedRequest: For the research router only; an agent it spawned ignores this and does its own task. A researcher message asking for one thing (one record such as a birth, marriage, death or census entry, or when or where one event happened; a person's children or siblings, or whether they are complete; a transcription; a letter; a review of attached sources) is a bounded request. A message that asks to research something else instead of the project's current question is not one: it is a different question (research/SKILL.md, "A genuinely different question"). A bounded request's owning agent runs in this turn, after init-project when there is no project yet, and the turn never runs question-selection. A bounded request that asks for more than one thing runs only the first one's agent this turn and names the rest. For a record, or for a person's children or siblings, that agent is search-records, and its turn ends on search-records' "Continue with …?" offer. For a review of attached sources that agent is source-evaluation, which reads them: the router reads none of them itself, and its turn ends on that review and an offer of the next step. A requested record that attachedSources already lists is not searched for: read it with person_read and name it. A children or siblings ask starts from what is attached: the brief tells search-records to read each census attached to the person with record_read before any search (tree_query gives each source's url, which record_read takes as recordId) and to name the household each shows.

quirks: The 1906 San Francisco earthquake and fire destroyed City Hall and the Hall of Records. Pre-1906 county-level civil birth, marriage, and death certificates were largely destroyed. Substitute sources (church records, funeral home records, Great Registers, newspapers) are essential for the entire 1850-1905 period.

San Francisco passenger arrival lists for approximately 1865-1892 are not digitized or name-indexed online. NARA microfilm reels (M261 and predecessor series) must be consulted in person at the National Archives at San Francisco (San Bruno, CA) or by mail request.

The Great Register (voter register) states each registrant's nativity, naturalization court, and naturalization date — the highest-priority substitute source when passenger lists and pre-1906 vital records are unavailable. FamilySearch collection 1935764 (3.3 million records, indexed) and Ancestry Voter Registers 1866-1898 (indexed + images).

Naturalization before 1880 was in the state district court (or county court 1862-1880); after 1880 in the superior court. San Francisco is also a federal district court seat, so many immigrants naturalized under the Northern District Court — covered by FamilySearch collection 1849982.

Declarations of intention (first papers) from the US Northern District Court 1846-1903 are at the National Archives, San Bruno (also FamilySearch Library films 977767-70). These may predate final citizenship by years and often name German hometown.
The 1900 census is the most direct online source for an immigrant's year of arrival — it asks for year of immigration and years in the US. The 1880 census records only birthplace.

North German surname Gaetjen (Low German patronymic, Oldenburg/Hannover/East Friesland region) — search Hamburg departure lists (Ancestry, partially indexed 1877-1914) as departure records often name the emigrant's home village. North Germans disproportionately used Hamburg over Bremen.

Bremen departure lists are largely destroyed; only 1907-1908 and 1913-1914 card index and a partial 1920-1939 reconstruction survive. Baltimore arrival lists partially compensate for Bremen-departing immigrants.

San Francisco funeral home records (FamilySearch collection 1385518, 162,363 records, indexed + images) survived 1906 and often record birthplace, parents' names, and informant — more detailed than civil death certificates.

The 1904 death certificate volumes (nine digitized volumes from FamilySearch volume search) are 0% name-indexed but full-text searchable — use FamilySearch full-text search to locate Gaetjen without browsing image by image.
Many original San Francisco cemeteries were relocated to Colma (San Mateo County) in the early 20th century — search San Mateo County records for burial information.
Search name variants: Gaetjen, Gaetgen, Gätjen, Gärtjen, and anglicized or misspelled forms with plain a or e instead of ae/ä.

response.objective: Trace John Carter (b. ~1836, Leeds, Yorkshire), husband of Ann, and their children in the Leeds census and parish records.
response.boundedRequest: For the research router only; an agent it spawned ignores this and does its own task. A researcher message asking for one thing (one record such as a birth, marriage, death or census entry, or when or where one event happened; a person's children or siblings, or whether they are complete; a transcription; a letter; a review of attached sources) is a bounded request. A message that asks to research something else instead of the project's current question is not one: it is a different question (research/SKILL.md, "A genuinely different question"). A bounded request's owning agent runs in this turn, after init-project when there is no project yet, and the turn never runs question-selection. A bounded request that asks for more than one thing runs only the first one's agent this turn and names the rest. For a record, or for a person's children or siblings, that agent is search-records, and its turn ends on search-records' "Continue with …?" offer. For a review of attached sources that agent is source-evaluation, which reads them: the router reads none of them itself, and its turn ends on that review and an offer of the next step. A requested record that attachedSources already lists is not searched for: read it with person_read and name it. A children or siblings ask starts from what is attached: the brief tells search-records to read each census attached to the person with record_read before any search (tree_query gives each source's url, which record_read takes as recordId) and to name the household each shows.

The name is an exact match (Patrick Flynn), and the death certificate gives a birth year of about 1845 against the tree's ~1845. The residence is the same county: Schuylkill, where the 1850 and 1860 census links (pe_001, pe_004) place him. Those census links are independent of this certificate, and they carry the identity. The birthplace conflict (certificate says Pennsylvania, tree and censuses say Ireland) is already settled as c_001, so it does not lower the tier.

**What does not hold up.**
- The rationale cites the death date and place as a match. The tree's Death fact (F2, 1908-03-12, Schuylkill) is sourced only to S3, which is this same certificate (src_004). That agreement is circular and adds no corroboration.

- It does not mention the birthplace conflict or the settlement of c_001.

response.boundedRequest: For the research router only; an agent it spawned ignores this and does its own task. A researcher message asking for one thing (one record such as a birth, marriage, death or census entry, or when or where one event happened; a person's children or siblings, or whether they are complete; a transcription; a letter; a review of attached sources) is a bounded request. A message that asks to research something else instead of the project's current question is not one: it is a different question (research/SKILL.md, "A genuinely different question"). A bounded request's owning agent runs in this turn, after init-project when there is no project yet, and the turn never runs question-selection. A bounded request that asks for more than one thing runs only the first one's agent this turn and names the rest. For a record, or for a person's children or siblings, that agent is search-records, and its turn ends on search-records' "Continue with …?" offer. For a review of attached sources that agent is source-evaluation, which reads them: the router reads none of them itself, and its turn ends on that review and an offer of the next step. A requested record that attachedSources already lists is not searched for: read it with person_read and name it. A children or siblings ask starts from what is attached: the brief tells search-records to read each census attached to the person with record_read before any search (tree_query gives each source's url, which record_read takes as recordId) and to name the household each shows.

response.boundedRequest: For the research router only; an agent it spawned ignores this and does its own task. A researcher message asking for one thing (one record such as a birth, marriage, death or census entry, or when or where one event happened; a person's children or siblings, or whether they are complete; a transcription; a letter; a review of attached sources) is a bounded request. A message that asks to research something else instead of the project's current question is not one: it is a different question (research/SKILL.md, "A genuinely different question"). A bounded request's owning agent runs in this turn, after init-project when there is no project yet, and the turn never runs question-selection. A bounded request that asks for more than one thing runs only the first one's agent this turn and names the rest. For a record, or for a person's children or siblings, that agent is search-records, and its turn ends on search-records' "Continue with …?" offer. For a review of attached sources that agent is source-evaluation, which reads them: the router reads none of them itself, and its turn ends on that review and an offer of the next step. A requested record that attachedSources already lists is not searched for: read it with person_read and name it. A children or siblings ask starts from what is attached: the brief tells search-records to read each census attached to the person with record_read before any search (tree_query gives each source's url, which record_read takes as recordId) and to name the household each shows.

response.boundedRequest: For the research router only; an agent it spawned ignores this and does its own task. A researcher message asking for one thing (one record such as a birth, marriage, death or census entry, or when or where one event happened; a person's children or siblings, or whether they are complete; a transcription; a letter; a review of attached sources) is a bounded request. A message that asks to research something else instead of the project's current question is not one: it is a different question (research/SKILL.md, "A genuinely different question"). A bounded request's owning agent runs in this turn, after init-project when there is no project yet, and the turn never runs question-selection. A bounded request that asks for more than one thing runs only the first one's agent this turn and names the rest. For a record, or for a person's children or siblings, that agent is search-records, and its turn ends on search-records' "Continue with …?" offer. For a review of attached sources that agent is source-evaluation, which reads them: the router reads none of them itself, and its turn ends on that review and an offer of the next step. A requested record that attachedSources already lists is not searched for: read it with person_read and name it. A children or siblings ask starts from what is attached: the brief tells search-records to read each census attached to the person with record_read before any search (tree_query gives each source's url, which record_read takes as recordId) and to name the household each shows.

response.boundedRequest: For the research router only; an agent it spawned ignores this and does its own task. A researcher message asking for one thing (one record such as a birth, marriage, death or census entry, or when or where one event happened; a person's children or siblings, or whether they are complete; a transcription; a letter; a review of attached sources) is a bounded request. A message that asks to research something else instead of the project's current question is not one: it is a different question (research/SKILL.md, "A genuinely different question"). A bounded request's owning agent runs in this turn, after init-project when there is no project yet, and the turn never runs question-selection. A bounded request that asks for more than one thing runs only the first one's agent this turn and names the rest. For a record, or for a person's children or siblings, that agent is search-records, and its turn ends on search-records' "Continue with …?" offer. For a review of attached sources that agent is source-evaluation, which reads them: the router reads none of them itself, and its turn ends on that review and an offer of the next step. A requested record that attachedSources already lists is not searched for: read it with person_read and name it. A children or siblings ask starts from what is attached: the brief tells search-records to read each census attached to the person with record_read before any search (tree_query gives each source's url, which record_read takes as recordId) and to name the household each shows.

response.boundedRequest: For the research router only; an agent it spawned ignores this and does its own task. A researcher message asking for one thing (one record such as a birth, marriage, death or census entry, or when or where one event happened; a person's children or siblings, or whether they are complete; a transcription; a letter; a review of attached sources) is a bounded request. A message that asks to research something else instead of the project's current question is not one: it is a different question (research/SKILL.md, "A genuinely different question"). A bounded request's owning agent runs in this turn, after init-project when there is no project yet, and the turn never runs question-selection. A bounded request that asks for more than one thing runs only the first one's agent this turn and names the rest. For a record, or for a person's children or siblings, that agent is search-records, and its turn ends on search-records' "Continue with …?" offer. For a review of attached sources that agent is source-evaluation, which reads them: the router reads none of them itself, and its turn ends on that review and an offer of the next step. A requested record that attachedSources already lists is not searched for: read it with person_read and name it. A children or siblings ask starts from what is attached: the brief tells search-records to read each census attached to the person with record_read before any search (tree_query gives each source's url, which record_read takes as recordId) and to name the household each shows.

response.objective: I am trying to find evidence of the immigration of Hermann Gaetjen to the United States from Germany between 1850 and 1878; he was married to Amelia Nichols.
response.boundedRequest: For the research router only; an agent it spawned ignores this and does its own task. A researcher message asking for one thing (one record such as a birth, marriage, death or census entry, or when or where one event happened; a person's children or siblings, or whether they are complete; a transcription; a letter; a review of attached sources) is a bounded request. A message that asks to research something else instead of the project's current question is not one: it is a different question (research/SKILL.md, "A genuinely different question"). A bounded request's owning agent runs in this turn, after init-project when there is no project yet, and the turn never runs question-selection. A bounded request that asks for more than one thing runs only the first one's agent this turn and names the rest. For a record, or for a person's children or siblings, that agent is search-records, and its turn ends on search-records' "Continue with …?" offer. For a review of attached sources that agent is source-evaluation, which reads them: the router reads none of them itself, and its turn ends on that review and an offer of the next step. A requested record that attachedSources already lists is not searched for: read it with person_read and name it. A children or siblings ask starts from what is attached: the brief tells search-records to read each census attached to the person with record_read before any search (tree_query gives each source's url, which record_read takes as recordId) and to name the household each shows.

quirks: The 1906 San Francisco earthquake and fire destroyed City Hall and the Hall of Records. Pre-1906 county-level civil birth, marriage, and death certificates were largely destroyed. Substitute sources (church records, funeral home records, Great Registers, newspapers) are essential for the entire 1850-1905 period.

San Francisco passenger arrival lists for approximately 1865-1892 are not digitized or name-indexed online. NARA microfilm reels (M261 and predecessor series) must be consulted in person at the National Archives at San Francisco (San Bruno, CA) or by mail request.

The Great Register (voter register) states each registrant's nativity, naturalization court, and naturalization date — the highest-priority substitute source when passenger lists and pre-1906 vital records are unavailable. FamilySearch collection 1935764 (3.3 million records, indexed) and Ancestry Voter Registers 1866-1898 (indexed + images).

Naturalization before 1880 was in the state district court (or county court 1862-1880); after 1880 in the superior court. San Francisco is also a federal district court seat, so many immigrants naturalized under the Northern District Court — covered by FamilySearch collection 1849982.

Declarations of intention (first papers) from the US Northern District Court 1846-1903 are at the National Archives, San Bruno (also FamilySearch Library films 977767-70). These may predate final citizenship by years and often name German hometown.
The 1900 census is the most direct online source for an immigrant's year of arrival — it asks for year of immigration and years in the US. The 1880 census records only birthplace.

Bremen departure lists are largely destroyed; only 1907-1908 and 1913-1914 card index and a partial 1920-1939 reconstruction survive. Baltimore arrival lists partially compensate for Bremen-departing immigrants.

San Francisco funeral home records (FamilySearch collection 1385518, 162,363 records, indexed + images) survived 1906 and often record birthplace, parents' names, and informant — more detailed than civil death certificates.

The 1904 death certificate volumes (nine digitized volumes from FamilySearch volume search) are 0% name-indexed but full-text searchable — use FamilySearch full-text search to locate Gaetjen without browsing image by image.
Many original San Francisco cemeteries were relocated to Colma (San Mateo County) in the early 20th century — search San Mateo County records for burial information.
Search name variants: Gaetjen, Gaetgen, Gätjen, Gärtjen, and anglicized or misspelled forms with plain a or e instead of ae/ä.

quirks: The 1906 San Francisco earthquake and fire destroyed City Hall and the Hall of Records. Pre-1906 county-level civil birth, marriage, and death certificates were largely destroyed. Substitute sources (church records, funeral home records, Great Registers, newspapers) are essential for the entire 1850-1905 period.

San Francisco passenger arrival lists for approximately 1865-1892 are not digitized or name-indexed online. NARA microfilm reels (M261 and predecessor series) must be consulted in person at the National Archives at San Francisco (San Bruno, CA) or by mail request.

The Great Register (voter register) states each registrant's nativity, naturalization court, and naturalization date — the highest-priority substitute source when passenger lists and pre-1906 vital records are unavailable. FamilySearch collection 1935764 (3.3 million records, indexed) and Ancestry Voter Registers 1866-1898 (indexed + images).

Naturalization before 1880 was in the state district court (or county court 1862-1880); after 1880 in the superior court. San Francisco is also a federal district court seat, so many immigrants naturalized under the Northern District Court — covered by FamilySearch collection 1849982.

Declarations of intention (first papers) from the US Northern District Court 1846-1903 are at the National Archives, San Bruno (also FamilySearch Library films 977767-70). These may predate final citizenship by years and often name German hometown.
The 1900 census is the most direct online source for an immigrant's year of arrival — it asks for year of immigration and years in the US. The 1880 census records only birthplace.

North German surname Gaetjen (Low German patronymic, Oldenburg/Hannover/East Friesland region) — search Hamburg departure lists (Ancestry, partially indexed 1877-1914) as departure records often name the emigrant's home village. North Germans disproportionately used Hamburg over Bremen.

Bremen departure lists are largely destroyed; only 1907-1908 and 1913-1914 card index and a partial 1920-1939 reconstruction survive. Baltimore arrival lists partially compensate for Bremen-departing immigrants.

San Francisco funeral home records (FamilySearch collection 1385518, 162,363 records, indexed + images) survived 1906 and often record birthplace, parents' names, and informant — more detailed than civil death certificates.

The 1904 death certificate volumes (nine digitized volumes from FamilySearch volume search) are 0% name-indexed but full-text searchable — use FamilySearch full-text search to locate Gaetjen without browsing image by image.
Many original San Francisco cemeteries were relocated to Colma (San Mateo County) in the early 20th century — search San Mateo County records for burial information.
Search name variants: Gaetjen, Gaetgen, Gätjen, Gärtjen, and anglicized or misspelled forms with plain a or e instead of ae/ä.

response.boundedRequest: For the research router only; an agent it spawned ignores this and does its own task. A researcher message asking for one thing (one record such as a birth, marriage, death or census entry, or when or where one event happened; a person's children or siblings, or whether they are complete; a transcription; a letter; a review of attached sources) is a bounded request. A message that asks to research something else instead of the project's current question is not one: it is a different question (research/SKILL.md, "A genuinely different question"). A bounded request's owning agent runs in this turn, after init-project when there is no project yet, and the turn never runs question-selection. A bounded request that asks for more than one thing runs only the first one's agent this turn and names the rest. For a record, or for a person's children or siblings, that agent is search-records, and its turn ends on search-records' "Continue with …?" offer. For a review of attached sources that agent is source-evaluation, which reads them: the router reads none of them itself, and its turn ends on that review and an offer of the next step. A requested record that attachedSources already lists is not searched for: read it with person_read and name it. A children or siblings ask starts from what is attached: the brief tells search-records to read each census attached to the person with record_read before any search (tree_query gives each source's url, which record_read takes as recordId) and to name the household each shows.

response.boundedRequest: For the research router only; an agent it spawned ignores this and does its own task. A researcher message asking for one thing (one record such as a birth, marriage, death or census entry, or when or where one event happened; a person's children or siblings, or whether they are complete; a transcription; a letter; a review of attached sources) is a bounded request. A message that asks to research something else instead of the project's current question is not one: it is a different question (research/SKILL.md, "A genuinely different question"). A bounded request's owning agent runs in this turn, after init-project when there is no project yet, and the turn never runs question-selection. A bounded request that asks for more than one thing runs only the first one's agent this turn and names the rest. For a record, or for a person's children or siblings, that agent is search-records, and its turn ends on search-records' "Continue with …?" offer. For a review of attached sources that agent is source-evaluation, which reads them: the router reads none of them itself, and its turn ends on that review and an offer of the next step. A requested record that attachedSources already lists is not searched for: read it with person_read and name it. A children or siblings ask starts from what is attached: the brief tells search-records to read each census attached to the person with record_read before any search (tree_query gives each source's url, which record_read takes as recordId) and to name the household each shows.

response.boundedRequest: For the research router only; an agent it spawned ignores this and does its own task. A researcher message asking for one thing (one record such as a birth, marriage, death or census entry, or when or where one event happened; a person's children or siblings, or whether they are complete; a transcription; a letter; a review of attached sources) is a bounded request. A message that asks to research something else instead of the project's current question is not one: it is a different question (research/SKILL.md, "A genuinely different question"). A bounded request's owning agent runs in this turn, after init-project when there is no project yet, and the turn never runs question-selection. A bounded request that asks for more than one thing runs only the first one's agent this turn and names the rest. For a record, or for a person's children or siblings, that agent is search-records, and its turn ends on search-records' "Continue with …?" offer. For a review of attached sources that agent is source-evaluation, which reads them: the router reads none of them itself, and its turn ends on that review and an offer of the next step. A requested record that attachedSources already lists is not searched for: read it with person_read and name it. A children or siblings ask starts from what is attached: the brief tells search-records to read each census attached to the person with record_read before any search (tree_query gives each source's url, which record_read takes as recordId) and to name the household each shows.

response.boundedRequest: For the research router only; an agent it spawned ignores this and does its own task. A researcher message asking for one thing (one record such as a birth, marriage, death or census entry, or when or where one event happened; a person's children or siblings, or whether they are complete; a transcription; a letter; a review of attached sources) is a bounded request. A message that asks to research something else instead of the project's current question is not one: it is a different question (research/SKILL.md, "A genuinely different question"). A bounded request's owning agent runs in this turn, after init-project when there is no project yet, and the turn never runs question-selection. A bounded request that asks for more than one thing runs only the first one's agent this turn and names the rest. For a record, or for a person's children or siblings, that agent is search-records, and its turn ends on search-records' "Continue with …?" offer. For a review of attached sources that agent is source-evaluation, which reads them: the router reads none of them itself, and its turn ends on that review and an offer of the next step. A requested record that attachedSources already lists is not searched for: read it with person_read and name it. A children or siblings ask starts from what is attached: the brief tells search-records to read each census attached to the person with record_read before any search (tree_query gives each source's url, which record_read takes as recordId) and to name the household each shows.

response.boundedRequest: For the research router only; an agent it spawned ignores this and does its own task. A researcher message asking for one thing (one record such as a birth, marriage, death or census entry, or when or where one event happened; a person's children or siblings, or whether they are complete; a transcription; a letter; a review of attached sources) is a bounded request. A message that asks to research something else instead of the project's current question is not one: it is a different question (research/SKILL.md, "A genuinely different question"). A bounded request's owning agent runs in this turn, after init-project when there is no project yet, and the turn never runs question-selection. A bounded request that asks for more than one thing runs only the first one's agent this turn and names the rest. For a record, or for a person's children or siblings, that agent is search-records, and its turn ends on search-records' "Continue with …?" offer. For a review of attached sources that agent is source-evaluation, which reads them: the router reads none of them itself, and its turn ends on that review and an offer of the next step. A requested record that attachedSources already lists is not searched for: read it with person_read and name it. A children or siblings ask starts from what is attached: the brief tells search-records to read each census attached to the person with record_read before any search (tree_query gives each source's url, which record_read takes as recordId) and to name the household each shows.

response.boundedRequest: For the research router only; an agent it spawned ignores this and does its own task. A researcher message asking for one thing (one record such as a birth, marriage, death or census entry, or when or where one event happened; a person's children or siblings, or whether they are complete; a transcription; a letter; a review of attached sources) is a bounded request. A message that asks to research something else instead of the project's current question is not one: it is a different question (research/SKILL.md, "A genuinely different question"). A bounded request's owning agent runs in this turn, after init-project when there is no project yet, and the turn never runs question-selection. A bounded request that asks for more than one thing runs only the first one's agent this turn and names the rest. For a record, or for a person's children or siblings, that agent is search-records, and its turn ends on search-records' "Continue with …?" offer. For a review of attached sources that agent is source-evaluation, which reads them: the router reads none of them itself, and its turn ends on that review and an offer of the next step. A requested record that attachedSources already lists is not searched for: read it with person_read and name it. A children or siblings ask starts from what is attached: the brief tells search-records to read each census attached to the person with record_read before any search (tree_query gives each source's url, which record_read takes as recordId) and to name the household each shows.

Both census households are linked to the tree family, all at `probable`. The England-to-Tennessee move is unexplained, so none can go higher.

**Links written (22 `pe_` entries, pe_001 to pe_022):**
- **1870 Maury County household (src_001):** William (I1), Mary (I2), James (I3), Ellen (I4) and George (I5) each linked from every assertion on their persona, plus William's residence. All five birth-year checks give a gap of 0 years, and all five match score 0.78.
- **1880 Maury County household (src_002):** William (I1), Mary (I2) and George (I5) linked the same way. The wife and son relationship assertions are linked to both parties. Score 0.78 throughout.
- **Why `probable`:** the tree places the family in Horsham, Sussex, England in 1851 and 1861. Maury, Tennessee is about 6,804 km (4,228 miles) away. The Tennessee Emigration and Immigration wiki page names only the origins of pre-statehood settlers, not an arrival from England, and no passenger list, naturalization or other bridging record is in the project. Every link therefore carries that cap.
- **Edges:** I did not write new Couple or ParentChild edges. The tree already holds them from the 1861 Horsham census.

**Household check:** James (about 1852) and Ellen (about 1855) appear in 1870 but not in 1880, and the tree gives neither a death before 1880. They are absent in 1880, which is an open identity question. They may have left home, died, or be enumerated elsewhere.

**Materialized:** the 1870 and 1880 facts were written onto I1 to I5. The Tennessee residences were added as new facts. No conflicts surfaced.

**Warnings:** `person_warnings` on I1 to I5 returned only "implausible" nonStandardPlace notices on the Horsham and Maury residence facts. They are not impossibilities.

**Question status:** q_001 is not concluded. A proof-conclusion step is needed, and it must decide whether the move is bridged before the links can go higher.

**Next step:** either find a passenger list, naturalization, or other record of the move to England-born William in the project, or accept the `probable` tier and let proof-conclusion weigh it.

James and Ellen appear in 1870 but not in 1880, which is an open question. response.boundedRequest: For the research router only; an agent it spawned ignores this and does its own task. A researcher message asking for one thing (one record such as a birth, marriage, death or census entry, or when or where one event happened; a person's children or siblings, or whether they are complete; a transcription; a letter; a review of attached sources) is a bounded request. A message that asks to research something else instead of the project's current question is not one: it is a different question (research/SKILL.md, "A genuinely different question"). A bounded request's owning agent runs in this turn, after init-project when there is no project yet, and the turn never runs question-selection. A bounded request that asks for more than one thing runs only the first one's agent this turn and names the rest. For a record, or for a person's children or siblings, that agent is search-records, and its turn ends on search-records' "Continue with …?" offer. For a review of attached sources that agent is source-evaluation, which reads them: the router reads none of them itself, and its turn ends on that review and an offer of the next step. A requested record that attachedSources already lists is not searched for: read it with person_read and name it. A children or siblings ask starts from what is attached: the brief tells search-records to read each census attached to the person with record_read before any search (tree_query gives each source's url, which record_read takes as recordId) and to name the household each shows.
